un.hook: Something unsafe is not safe and someone unkind is not kind: un- means not.

apply1.prompt: An unbiased judge is one who is:
apply1.tip: Un- means not, so unbiased means not biased. An unbiased judge does not favor either side.

apply2.prompt: If a puzzle is unsolvable, it:
apply2.tip: Un- means not, and solvable means able to be solved, so unsolvable means not able to be solved.

re.hook: You rewind a video to go back and replay a game to play it again: re- means again or back.

apply1.prompt: To reconsider a decision is to:
apply1.tip: Re- means again, and consider means think about, so to reconsider is to think about something again.

apply2.prompt: When floodwaters recede, they:
apply2.tip: Re- means back, and cede comes from a Latin word meaning go, so water that recedes goes back.

pre.hook: You preheat an oven before you bake, and a prefix comes before a word: pre- means before.

apply1.prompt: A prehistoric animal lived:
apply1.tip: Pre- means before, so prehistoric means from the time before history was written down.

apply2.prompt: A precaution is something you do:
apply2.tip: Pre- means before, and caution means care, so a precaution is care you take before something can go wrong.

dis.hook: If you dislike something, you do not like it, and to disassemble a toy is to take it apart: dis- means not or apart.

apply1.prompt: A dishonest person is:
apply1.tip: Dis- means not, so dishonest means not honest, or not truthful.

apply2.prompt: When a crowd disperses, the people:
apply2.tip: Dis- means apart, and sperse comes from a Latin word meaning scatter, so a crowd that disperses scatters apart.

mis.hook: If you misplace your keys, you put them in the wrong place: mis- means wrong or badly.

apply1.prompt: To misjudge a distance is to:
apply1.tip: Mis- means wrongly, and judge means estimate or decide, so to misjudge is to estimate wrongly.

apply2.prompt: To mispronounce a word is to:
apply2.tip: Mis- means wrongly, and pronounce means say, so to mispronounce a word is to say it wrongly.

less.hook: A homeless dog is without a home and a sleepless night is without sleep: -less means without.

apply1.prompt: A cloudless sky is:
apply1.tip: Cloud plus -less, which means without, gives cloudless: a sky without any clouds.

apply2.prompt: A relentless storm is one that:
apply2.tip: To relent is to ease up, and -less means without, so relentless means without ever easing up.

ful.hook: A handful is what fills your hand, and a cheerful friend is full of cheer: -ful means full of.

apply1.prompt: A boastful person is:
apply1.tip: To boast is to brag, and -ful means full of, so a boastful person is full of bragging.

apply2.prompt: A deceitful plan is:
apply2.tip: Deceit means trickery, and -ful means full of, so a deceitful plan is full of trickery.

able.hook: Washable clothes can be washed and a readable note can be read: -able and -ible mean able to be.

apply1.prompt: Edible berries are able to be:
apply1.tip: Ed comes from a Latin word meaning eat, and -ible means able to be, so edible means able to be eaten.

apply2.prompt: Legible handwriting is able to be:
apply2.tip: Leg comes from a Latin word meaning read, and -ible means able to be, so legible means able to be read.

bene.hook: A benefit is something that is good for you: bene- means good or well.

apply1.prompt: A benefactor is a person who:
apply1.tip: Bene- means good, and fact comes from a Latin word meaning do, so a benefactor does good for others.

apply2.prompt: A beneficial habit is one that is:
apply2.tip: Bene- means good, so something beneficial does good for you or helps you.

mal.hook: A malfunction is when a machine works wrong, and malpractice is bad work by a doctor: mal- means bad or wrong.

apply1.prompt: A malnourished child has:
apply1.tip: Mal- means bad, and nourished means fed, so a malnourished child is badly fed and has poor nutrition.

apply2.prompt: A malodorous room is one that:
apply2.tip: Mal- means bad, and odor means smell, so a malodorous room has a bad smell.

sub.hook: A submarine travels under the sea, and a subtitle sits below the picture: sub- means under or below.

apply1.prompt: A subterranean cave is located:
apply1.tip: Sub- means under, and terra is Latin for earth, so subterranean means under the ground.

apply2.prompt: A subordinate at work is someone who:
apply2.tip: Sub- means below, and ordinate comes from a word for rank or order, so a subordinate ranks below someone else.

inter.hook: An interstate highway runs between states, and an intermission comes between acts of a play: inter- means between or among.

apply1.prompt: An intermediary is someone who:
apply1.tip: Inter- means between, and medi means middle, so an intermediary stands in the middle between two sides.

apply2.prompt: Interstellar travel takes place:
apply2.tip: Inter- means between, and stellar means of the stars, so interstellar means between the stars.

trans.hook: A transatlantic flight goes across the Atlantic, and transparent glass lets light pass through: trans- means across or through.

apply1.prompt: A transcontinental railroad runs:
apply1.tip: Trans- means across, so a transcontinental railroad runs across a whole continent.

apply2.prompt: A translucent curtain is one that:
apply2.tip: Trans- means through, and luc comes from a Latin word meaning shine, so light shines through something translucent.

in.hook: Something incorrect is not correct, and someone impolite is not polite: in- and im- mean not.

apply1.prompt: An inaudible whisper is one that is:
apply1.tip: In- means not, and audible means able to be heard, so an inaudible whisper cannot be heard.

apply2.prompt: An immobile statue is one that:
apply2.tip: Im- means not, and mobile means able to move, so something immobile is not able to move.

dict.hook: A dictionary tells you what words mean and how to say them: dict means say or speak.

apply1.prompt: A singer with clear diction:
apply1.tip: Dict means say or speak, so diction is the way a person says or pronounces words.

apply2.prompt: To contradict a friend is to:
apply2.tip: Contra means against, and dict means say, so to contradict is to say something against what another person said.

scrib.hook: You scribble with a pencil, and actors follow a script in a play: scrib and script mean write.

apply1.prompt: To inscribe a ring is to:
apply1.tip: In- means into, and scrib means write, so to inscribe a ring is to write or carve words into it.

apply2.prompt: A prescription is something a doctor:
apply2.tip: Pre- means before, and script means write, so a prescription is written before you can get your medicine.

spect.hook: Spectacles help you see, and a spectacular show is amazing to look at: spect means look or see.

apply1.prompt: To think about an event in retrospect is to:
apply1.tip: Retro means back, and spect means look, so in retrospect means looking back on something.

apply2.prompt: A person who enjoys introspection likes to:
apply2.tip: Intro means inward, and spect means look, so introspection is looking inward at your own thoughts.

port.hook: A hotel porter carries your bags, and imports are goods carried into a country: port means carry.

apply1.prompt: A portfolio is a case for:
apply1.tip: Port means carry, and folio means sheet of paper, so a portfolio is a case for carrying papers.

apply2.prompt: To deport someone is to:
apply2.answer: send them out of the country
apply2.tip: De- means away, and port means carry, so to deport someone is to carry or send them away from a country.

voc.hook: Your vocal cords make your voice, and a vocation is work you feel called to do: voc means voice or call.

apply1.prompt: A vociferous crowd is one that is:
apply1.tip: Vociferous comes from voc, voice. A vociferous crowd uses its voices loudly. Don't mix voc up with vis, which means see.

apply2.prompt: To revoke a permission is to:
apply2.tip: Revoke is re (back) plus vok (call). When you revoke something, you call it back.

duc.hook: A conductor leads an orchestra and an aqueduct leads water to a city: duc and duct mean lead.

apply1.prompt: A medicine that induces sleep:
apply1.tip: Induce is in (into) plus duc (lead). Something that induces sleep leads you into sleep. Don't confuse duc with dict, which means say.

apply2.prompt: A duct in a building is a pipe or channel that:
apply2.answer: leads air from place to place
apply2.tip: Duct comes from duct, lead. A duct leads air or water from one place to another.

chron.hook: A chronometer measures time exactly, and a chronic cough lasts a long time: chron means time.

apply1.prompt: To synchronize two watches is to:
apply1.answer: set them to the same time
apply1.tip: Synchronize is syn (together) plus chron (time) plus ize (make). You make the watches show the same time. Chrom means color.

apply2.prompt: An anachronism is something that:
apply2.answer: is placed in the wrong time
wrong: is placed in the wrong country
is told in the wrong voice
apply2.tip: Anachronism holds chron, time. An anachronism is out of its time, like a cell phone in a story about knights.

bio.hook: Biology is the study of life, and an antibiotic fights tiny living germs: bio means life.

apply1.prompt: Biodegradable trash is trash that:
apply1.answer: is broken down by living things
wrong: is broken down by sunlight alone
apply1.tip: Biodegradable is bio (life) plus degrade (break down). Living things like bacteria break it down. Geo, not bio, means earth.

apply2.prompt: A biome is a large area known for its:
apply2.tip: Biome starts with bio, life. A biome, like a desert or rainforest, is defined by the living things found there.

geo.hook: Geography maps the earth, and a geode is a rock you crack open from the ground: geo means earth.

apply1.prompt: Geothermal energy comes from:
apply1.tip: Geothermal is geo (earth) plus therm (heat). It is heat from inside the earth. Bio, not geo, means life.

apply2.prompt: In a geocentric model of space, what is at the center?
apply2.tip: Geocentric is geo (earth) plus centric (center). A geocentric model puts the earth in the middle.

graph.hook: When you sign an autograph you write your name, and a graph draws numbers as a picture: graph means write or draw.

apply1.prompt: Calligraphy is the art of:
apply1.tip: Calligraphy is calli (beautiful) plus graph (write). It means beautiful writing. Phon, not graph, means sound.

apply2.prompt: A seismograph is a machine that:
apply2.tip: Seismograph is seism (earthquake) plus graph (write or draw). It draws lines that record how the ground shakes.

phon.hook: A telephone carries your voice far away, and a microphone picks up sound: phon means sound.

apply1.prompt: A cacophony is a mix of:
apply1.tip: Cacophony is caco (bad) plus phon (sound). A cacophony is a mix of harsh, unpleasant sounds. Vis means see, not hear.

apply2.prompt: Two homophones are words that:
apply2.tip: Homophone is homo (same) plus phon (sound). Homophones like bear and bare sound alike. Graph would point to spelling.

ped.hook: You push bicycle pedals with your feet, and a tripod stands on three feet: ped and pod mean foot.

apply1.prompt: A pedicure is care for your:
apply1.tip: Pedicure is ped (foot) plus cure (care). It is care for your feet. Manu means hand, as in manicure.

apply2.prompt: A quadruped is an animal that walks on:
apply2.tip: Quadruped is quadr (four) plus ped (foot). A dog or horse is a quadruped because it walks on four feet.

man.hook: A manual car shifts gears by hand, and a manicure makes your hands look neat: man means hand.

apply1.prompt: Long ago, manuscripts were books that were:
apply1.tip: Manuscript is manu (hand) plus script (write). A manuscript was written by hand.

apply2.prompt: To manipulate clay is to:
apply2.tip: Manipulate starts with man, hand. When you manipulate clay, you handle and shape it. Ped, not man, means foot.

path.hook: You feel sympathy for a friend who is sad, and apathy means feeling nothing: path means feeling.

apply1.prompt: Telepathy is the idea of sharing:
apply1.answer: thoughts and feelings at a distance
wrong: sounds and voices at a distance
letters and notes at a distance
pictures and maps at a distance
apply1.tip: Telepathy is tele (far) plus path (feeling). It is sensing another person's feelings or thoughts from far away. Phon means sound.

apply2.prompt: Antipathy toward someone is a feeling of:
apply2.tip: Antipathy is anti (against) plus path (feeling). It is a feeling against someone, so it means strong dislike.

mono.hook: A unicycle has one wheel and a monorail runs on one track: mono- and uni- mean one.

apply1.prompt: A monolingual person speaks:
apply1.tip: Monolingual is mono (one) plus lingu (language). You speak just one language. Poly and multi mean many.

apply2.prompt: A unanimous vote is one in which:
apply2.tip: Unanimous is uni (one) plus anim (mind). In a unanimous vote, everyone is of one mind.

multi.hook: A multicolored shirt has many colors, and a polygon has many sides: multi- and poly- mean many.

apply1.prompt: A multitude of people is:
apply1.tip: Multitude starts with multi, many. A multitude is a huge number of people. Mono and uni mean one.

apply2.prompt: A polysyllabic word has:
apply2.tip: Polysyllabic is poly (many) plus syllabic (syllables). A word like encyclopedia is polysyllabic. Mono would mean one.

micro.hook: A microscope lets you see microbes, living things far too small to see with your eyes: micro- means small.

apply1.prompt: A microclimate is the weather of:
apply1.tip: Microclimate is micro (small) plus climate. It is the weather in one small spot, like a shady garden. Macro means large.

apply2.prompt: A micrometer is a tool that measures:
apply2.tip: Micrometer is micro (small) plus meter (measure). It measures tiny lengths, like the thickness of a wire.

auto.hook: An automatic door opens by itself, and an autograph is your name in your own hand: auto- means self.

apply1.prompt: An autonomous robot can:
apply1.tip: Autonomous is auto (self) plus nom (law or rule). An autonomous robot rules itself and acts without a person controlling it.

apply2.prompt: An autocrat is a ruler who:
apply2.tip: Autocrat is auto (self) plus crat (ruler). An autocrat rules by himself or herself, with no one sharing the power.

circum.hook: A circus ring goes around in a circle, and circumference is the distance around: circum- means around.

apply1.prompt: To circumnavigate the globe is to:
apply1.answer: sail all the way around it
apply1.tip: Circumnavigate is circum (around) plus navigate (sail). You travel all the way around. Trans, not circum, means across.

apply2.prompt: To circumvent a rule is to:
apply2.tip: Circumvent is circum (around) plus vent (come). You get around the rule instead of facing it. Contra means against.

contra.hook: A counterattack strikes back against an attack, and contrary people take the opposite side: contra- and counter- mean against.

apply1.prompt: Contraband is goods that are:
wrong: brought in with the law's approval
apply1.tip: Contraband is contra (against) plus band (a law or order). Contraband goods are smuggled in against the law.

apply2.prompt: A counterclockwise turn goes:
wrong: the same way as a clock's hands
apply2.tip: Counterclockwise is counter (against) plus clockwise. You turn the opposite way from the hands on a clock.

ify.hook: To simplify is to make simple, and to finalize is to make final: -ify and -ize mean to make.

apply1.prompt: To solidify a plan is to:
apply1.tip: Solidify is solid plus ify (to make). You make the plan solid, so it is firm and settled.

apply2.prompt: To fortify a castle is to:
apply2.tip: Fortify is fort (strong) plus ify (to make). When you fortify a castle, you make it stronger against attack.

er.hook: A painter is a person who paints and a cyclist is a person who cycles: -er, -or and -ist mean a person who.

apply1.prompt: A spectator is someone who:
apply1.tip: Spectator is spect (look) plus or (a person who). A spectator is a person who looks on and watches.

apply2.prompt: A botanist is a person who:
apply2.tip: Botanist is botan (plant) plus ist (a person who). A botanist is a person who studies plants. Geo would point to rocks.

aud.hook: You hear an audio clip, and an auditorium is a hall built for listening: aud means hear.

apply1.prompt: An auditory problem affects a person's ability to:
apply1.tip: Auditory comes from aud, which means hear. An auditory problem has to do with hearing, not seeing.

apply2.prompt: An audiologist is a specialist who checks your:
apply2.tip: Audio plus -logist, a person who studies. An audiologist studies and tests how well you hear.

mit.hook: When a teacher dismisses the class, you are sent out, and a missile is sent flying: mit and miss mean send.

apply1.prompt: To emit light or sound is to:
apply1.tip: E- means out and mit means send. When you emit something, you send it out.

apply2.prompt: An emissary is a person who is:
apply2.tip: Emissary contains miss, meaning send. An emissary is someone sent out to carry a message or do official business.

ous.hook: A joyous day is full of joy and a dangerous road is full of danger: -ous means full of.

apply1.prompt: A perilous journey is one that is:
apply1.tip: Peril means danger, and -ous means full of. So a perilous journey is full of danger.

apply2.prompt: A vigorous person is:
apply2.tip: Vigor means strength and energy, and -ous means full of. Don't mix it up with -less, which means without.

tion.hook: Celebration is the act of celebrating and confusion is the state of being confused: -tion and -sion name an act or state.

apply1.prompt: If to erode means to wear away, erosion is:
wrong: a person who wears things away
apply1.tip: Erode plus -sion makes erosion. The suffix turns the action into a thing: the act of wearing away.

apply2.prompt: If to exasperate means to annoy greatly, exasperation is:
apply2.tip: Exasperate plus -tion makes exasperation. The suffix names the state you are in: great annoyance.

anti.hook: Antibacterial soap fights germs and antifreeze works against freezing: anti- means against.

apply1.prompt: An antiwar protest is one that is:
apply1.tip: Anti- means against, so an antiwar protest is against war. Don't confuse it with ante-, which means before.

apply2.prompt: If you feel antipathy toward a plan, you feel:
apply2.tip: Anti- means against and path means feeling. Antipathy is a feeling against something, a strong dislike.

ex.hook: An exit is the way out and to exhale is to breathe out: ex- means out or away.

apply1.prompt: To expel a student is to:
wrong: move the student up a grade
apply1.tip: Ex- means out and pel means push. To expel someone is to push them out.

apply2.prompt: To excavate a site is to:
apply2.tip: Ex- means out, and cav means hollow, as in cave. To excavate is to hollow something out by digging.

de.hook: To defrost a freezer takes the ice away, and to dethrone a king brings him down: de- means down or away.

apply1.prompt: To demote a soldier is to:
apply1.tip: De- means down, and mote comes from move. To demote is to move someone down in rank. Promote is the opposite.

apply2.prompt: To dehydrate fruit is to:
apply2.answer: take the water out of it
apply2.tip: De- means away and hydr means water. To dehydrate something is to take its water away.

co.hook: Coworkers work together and to combine things puts them together: co-, com- and con- mean with or together.

apply1.prompt: Two events that coincide happen:
apply1.tip: Co- means together. Events that coincide happen together, at the same time.

apply2.prompt: When people congregate in a town square, they:
apply2.tip: Con- means together and greg means flock or group. To congregate is to flock together.

super.hook: Superhuman strength goes beyond normal strength and a supersonic jet flies faster than sound: super- means above or beyond.

apply1.prompt: Superfluous details are ones that are:
apply1.tip: Super- means beyond and flu means flow. Superfluous things overflow beyond what is needed. Don't confuse super- with sub-, meaning under.

apply2.prompt: To superimpose one picture on another is to:
apply2.tip: Super- means above and impose means to place on. To superimpose is to place one thing above another.

post.hook: A postgame show airs after the game and the postwar years came after a war: post- means after.

apply1.prompt: A postoperative patient is one who is:
apply1.tip: Post- means after, and operative refers to an operation. Postoperative means after surgery. Pre- would mean before.

apply2.prompt: A posthumous award is given:
apply2.tip: Post- means after. A posthumous award comes after the person's death.

fore.hook: Your forehead is the front of your head and the forecast tells you the weather before it comes: fore- means before or in front.

apply1.prompt: To forewarn someone is to:
apply1.tip: Fore- means before. To forewarn is to warn someone before something happens.

apply2.prompt: The foreground of a painting is the part that is:
apply2.tip: Fore- means in front. The foreground is the ground in front, the part of the scene nearest to you.

over.hook: If you overeat you eat too much, and if you oversleep you sleep too long: over- means too much.

apply1.prompt: An overzealous fan is one who is:
apply1.tip: Zealous means eager, and over- means too much. An overzealous fan is too eager. Under- would mean not enough.

apply2.prompt: To overexert yourself is to:
apply2.tip: To exert yourself is to put in effort. Over- means too much, so to overexert is to push yourself too hard.

vis.hook: Vision is your sense of sight and a video is something you watch: vis and vid mean see.

apply1.prompt: To envision your future is to:
apply1.tip: Envision contains vis, meaning see. To envision is to see something in your mind. Aud would be about hearing.

apply2.prompt: Evident proof is proof that:
apply2.tip: E- means out and vid means see. Evident proof stands out where you can clearly see it.

struct.hook: A construction crew builds roads, and destruction is the opposite of building: struct means build.

apply1.prompt: An obstruction in a pipe is something that:
apply1.tip: Ob- means against and struct means build. An obstruction is something built up against the flow, blocking it.

apply2.prompt: To reconstruct a bridge is to:
apply2.tip: Re- means again and struct means build. To reconstruct is to build again. Don't confuse struct with rupt, meaning break.

rupt.hook: A volcano erupts when lava breaks out, and a bankrupt business is financially broken: rupt means break.

apply1.prompt: A ruptured water pipe is one that has:
apply1.tip: Rupt means break. A ruptured pipe has broken or burst open.

apply2.prompt: Something that disrupts a meeting:
apply2.tip: Dis- means apart and rupt means break. To disrupt is to break something apart, like the flow of a meeting.

tract.hook: A tractor pulls a plow, and subtraction pulls numbers away: tract means pull or drag.

apply1.prompt: To retract a cat's claws is to:
apply1.tip: Re- means back and tract means pull. To retract is to pull back.

apply2.prompt: A protracted argument is one that is:
apply2.answer: dragged out for a long time
apply2.tip: Pro- means forward and tract means drag. A protracted argument is dragged on and on.

cred.hook: A bank gives you credit because it believes you will pay, and credentials make people believe you: cred means believe.

apply1.prompt: A credulous person is one who:
apply1.tip: Cred means believe and -ous means full of. A credulous person is full of belief and easily fooled.

apply2.prompt: To discredit a witness is to:
apply2.tip: Dis- means not or opposite, and cred means believe. To discredit someone is to make people not believe them.

ject.hook: A projector throws a picture onto a screen, and a projectile is thrown through the air: ject means throw.

apply1.prompt: To interject a comment is to:
wrong: pull it out of a conversation
apply1.tip: Inter- means between and ject means throw. To interject is to throw a comment in between what others say.

apply2.prompt: A dejected person feels:
apply2.tip: De- means down and ject means throw. A dejected person feels thrown down, low in spirits.
